1.explanation:
All of these modules participate in rendering, wiring up and tracking deep-link overlays for subprocesses:  
• DrilldownOverlayBehavior.js is responsible for drawing and updating the overlay icon on subprocess elements; if it doesn’t re-register overlays after loading a new diagram (global subprocess), the icon disappears.  
• SubprocessCompatibility.js adapts drilldown behavior to BPMN subprocess shapes — multi-diagram plugins can change how subprocess IDs or references are tracked, so compatibility code here may not pick up the new deep-link IDs.  
• DrilldownCentering.js recenters the viewport when drilling down or back up; if it doesn’t trigger a re-render or overlay update, the overlays aren’t re-attached.  
• DrilldownUtil.js contains shared utilities for identifying drilldown candidates and parsing deep-link URLs — if the URL parser or shape matcher isn’t aware of the global subprocess plugin’s naming conventions, it won’t re-activate overlays on subsequent diagrams.  
• PathMap.js builds the internal map between element IDs and their diagram paths (needed for deep linking). Multi-diagram mode extends the export/import of multiple BPMN diagrams, so PathMap must include entries for each global subprocess. If it only knows about the root diagram it cannot resolve the deep-link for nested subprocesses, and the overlay vanishes.
1.bug_scenario: When using the new deep-linking support for subprocesses together with a multi-diagram “global subprocess” plugin, the little overlay link icon that appears on the subprocess boundary is shown correctly for the first subprocess, but as soon as you navigate between subprocess diagrams (global subprocesses) the overlay vanishes and you can no longer click your way back. In other words, drill-down deep-links work only once in the root diagram and then stop appearing in nested or subsequent subprocess diagrams.

2.explanation:
All of these files implement the drill-down / deep-linking UI behavior and URL synchronization used when entering or leaving a subprocess: 

• DrilldownOverlayBehavior.js: renders and tears down the overlay around the subprocess shape when a deep link is activated or cleared.  
• DrilldownCentering.js: recenters the canvas on the target subprocess when navigating via URL.  
• DrilldownBreadcrumbs.js: manages the breadcrumb bar that allows the user to navigate back up the subprocess hierarchy.  
• SubprocessCompatibility.js: hooks into legacy subprocess semantics, ensuring overlays work on collapsed/folded subprocess shapes.  
• DrilldownUtil.js: contains utility functions for computing the drill-down path from the URL and locating the target element in the model.  
• NavigatedViewer.js: wires up URL fragment changes to the modeler/viewer instance, orchestrating the above behaviors on popstate/navigation.  

Because the multi-diagram plugin also drives view changes and overlays, these core drill-down files need to be adapted so that the overlay remains active across multi-diagram transitions and is not unmounted at the end of the animation.
2.bug_scenario: In the provided animation the user has two “global subprocess” shapes on the canvas and is using Camunda Modeler 5.0’s new deep‐linking support alongside a multi‐diagram plugin. When the user clicks the subprocess icon on the first subprocess, the drill‐down overlay appears correctly and the URL fragment is updated. However, as soon as they navigate to the second subprocess (or return), the drill‐down overlay is removed even though the URL fragment still points to the subprocess shape. In short: deep‐linking and the multi‐diagram navigation both vie for controlling the drill‐down overlay and the overlay is being dropped at the end of the transition.
